steps.question: Did this call show the agent the text of a local project file, which is the read tool's job? A project file is in the project's own tree (src/, crates/, packages/, docs/, or a named source or config file like package.json). Files downloaded or generated in the session, files under a run or scratch folder ($RUN, /tmp) and logs are not. YES: cat, head, tail, less, sed -n or awk given a project file path, or a Python or Node script that opened a project file and printed its text or a rewritten version of it. NO for everything else. In particular NO when head, tail, grep or sed only filtered another command's output; for running a program or script; searches (rg, grep), listings and counts (ls, find, wc, stat); git commands; builds, tests, linters, formatters and compilers; package managers; remote content (gh api, curl, wget); queries that select fields from structured data (jq, json.load(...)['key']); and binary files.

then.text: Chauffeur: Read project files with the read tool, not shell printers or Python/Node file reads, including scripts that print transformed source. Use build tools for compilation and edit or patch tools for changes.
